title: Kahlil Benson Surprises Chiefs in NFL Debut
seoTitle: Kahlil Benson surprises Chiefs in NFL debut
subtitle: The undrafted rookie solidified his role as blindside protection in a crucial game
excerpt: Undrafted rookie Kahlil Benson made a strong NFL debut, showcasing strength and consistency on the Kansas City Chiefs' offensive line, contributing to a key win.
author: Daniele Morais
contentHtml:
When the Kansas City Chiefs opened the season against the Denver Broncos, the absence of starting left tackle Josh Simmons, who was sidelined with a back injury, put undrafted rookie Kahlil Benson in the spotlight. In his debut, the Indiana native contained Nik Bonitto's pass rush, allowing only one pressure in 32 pass-blocking snaps.

Kahlil Benson Joins the Chiefs' Offensive Line

Benson joined the team as a tryout participant among more than 75 players and ultimately made the 53-man roster. In his first game, he stepped in at left tackle, facing one of the league's top pass rushers, and delivered the best performance among rookie OTs that week.

Performance Against Denver's Defense

Beyond blindside protection, Benson also excelled in run blocking, helping Kenneth Walker III achieve significant yardage in the game. His performance was considered one of the night's highlights, even with Patrick Mahomes, who was returning from a knee injury, not being as sharp as he usually is.

Confidence from Mahomes and Coaches

Patrick Mahomes expressed confidence in Benson, stating that he was ready to play and that the team trusts players who train hard to earn their spot. The quarterback acknowledged that mistakes can happen, but emphasized the importance of trusting the offensive line.

Impact on the Chiefs' Season

With Simmons' probable absence, Benson's debut could give the team more time to assess the starter's recovery and alleviate concerns about blindside protection, a critical point for the Chiefs. The rookie's performance might also influence recruitment decisions by other teams looking to bolster their offensive line.

Based on information from KC Kingdom, Heavy.com.
